common_name: Rainbow Candy Daylily (Purple-Banded Peach Candy-Series Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this tetraploid member of the Candy series needs a full season to settle in before producing its heaviest bud count.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Rainbow Candy produces large, creamy-peach flowers edged and banded in rich purple that deepens toward a lavender eye above a bold green throat. This tetraploid Candy-series cultivar carries a high bud count and blooms over an unusually long early-to-late-season window, giving weeks of color from a single clump. Deadhead spent scapes to tidy the planting and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Orchid Candy Daylily (Lavender Black-Eyed Candy-Series Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this compact tetraploid Candy-series cultivar suits the front of a border.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Orchid Candy bears orchid-lavender flowers marked with a striking black-purple eyezone above a green throat, held on compact scapes over a tidy, dormant clump. This tetraploid Candy-series cultivar blooms in a dependable midsummer flush and holds its color well through summer heat. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.

common_name: Boca Grande Daylily (Ruffled Gold-Orange Peach Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; semi-evergreen foliage benefits from a light winter mulch at the colder end of its range.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Boca Grande bears large, bright gold-orange-peach flowers nearly seven inches across with a ruffled petal edge and a clear green throat. This semi-evergreen cultivar blooms in a heavy midseason flush and reblooms later in summer rather than flowering just once. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; an old, long-lived heirloom cultivar that asks for little care once established.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Black Prince bears dark maroon-to-near-black, trumpet-shaped flowers with a subtle yellow throat on tall, sturdy scapes above dense, arching foliage. Each flower lasts only a day, but a long midsummer succession of buds keeps the clump in bloom for weeks. This heirloom cultivar, in circulation since the early 1940s, is easy-care in average soil and benefits from division every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Earl Porter Daylily (Near-Black Fragrant Reblooming Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; dormant foliage dies back cleanly in winter.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Earl Porter bears fragrant, near-black tetraploid flowers about five and a half inches across on well-branched, dormant scapes carrying a high bud count. It blooms in a strong midseason flush and reblooms later in summer rather than flowering just once. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; afternoon shade helps the darkest color hold longer into the day.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; Derrick Cane bears large red-black blend flowers with a yellow throat that open looking almost black in cooler morning light, though the intensity softens somewhat by late afternoon in hot sun. This cultivar blooms in an early-to-midseason flush and reblooms later in summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Dark Universe Daylily (Round Ruffled Black-Purple Self Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; a compact modern tetraploid suited to the front of a border.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Dark Universe bears round, ruffled, very dark red-purple-black self flowers with a tiny gold throat on compact, semi-evergreen scapes. This tetraploid cultivar blooms in midseason with dependable rebloom through summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous bloom.

common_name: Peacock Maiden Daylily (Giant Purple Spider Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; evergreen foliage benefits from winter protection at the colder end of its range.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Peacock Maiden produces enormous, fragrant purple spider-form flowers approaching ten inches across, with narrow, crispate petals surrounding a creamy white eyezone and a large green throat. This evergreen diploid carries an extended bloom habit, flowering over a long midsummer-to-late season window, and has been widely used as a hybridizing parent for later spider and unusual-form cultivars. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Heavenly Curls Daylily (Cascading Cream Spider Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; the long, cascading petals show best with some space around the clump.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Heavenly Curls bears large, creamy yellow to near-white spider-form flowers about seven inches across above a bright green throat, with long petals and sepals that curl and cascade to give each bloom an undulating, open form. This diploid cultivar blooms in midseason on scapes just over two feet tall. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.
